Its bounded tasks do not establish meaningful improvement at complete physical jobs. With no deadline and no decisive matching result, the compound forecast remains open.
limitations: Missing leaderboard entries are not zero scores.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Mythos will likely score under 20% (perhaps under 10%) on the Remote Labor Index, with no meaningful improvement on physical jobs.

statement.excerpt: My strong intuition is that Mythos will be under 20% and perhaps under 10% on the Remote Labor Index (a benchmark of percent of online tasks a bot can do), and with no meaningful improvement on doing physical jobs — which means the number of actual full human jobs that can be entirely replaced will remain small, at least for now.

from_speaker: no meaningful improvement on doing physical jobs
actual full human jobs that can be entirely replaced will remain small
our_interpretation: Treat under 20% as the main directional forecast despite its expressed uncertainty. Under 10% is a tentative stronger possibility, not a second firm threshold.
Mythos means the Mythos Preview version discussed on May 10. Scores for Fable, Opus, or later Mythos versions are not interchangeable.
Use RLI's automation rate for completed projects, not a general benchmark score or an estimate of jobs replaced.
The physical-jobs clause concerns practical occupational capability. Improvements on isolated robotics tasks are relevant but do not automatically demonstrate improved completion of whole jobs.
For now supplies no definite deadline. The full-jobs conclusion remains part of the assessment, although small has no numerical definition.
criteria.support_condition: An authenticated comparable RLI evaluation places the relevant Mythos Preview version below 20%, with evidence also supporting the stated lack of meaningful physical-job improvement and limited complete-job replacement.
criteria.contradiction_condition: A valid comparable RLI result is at least 20%, or direct practical evidence demonstrates meaningful physical-job improvement contrary to the forecast. Isolated task gains alone do not settle the complete-job claim.
